subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Which public provider-family fallback contract should OpenClaw support for model failover: wildcard/auto refs, explicit ordered fallback families, catalog-derived candidates, or no new core config surface?
rationale: This changes provider/model routing and config semantics, and current evidence shows multiple plausible contracts with different upgrade, cost-control, and operator-surprise tradeoffs.

options.title: Design explicit family fallback contract
options.body: Adopt an explicit ordered family/group contract, such as fallbackFamilies or equivalent, so users control provider and subscription-tier order without relying on ambiguous provider auto-selection.

options.title: Narrow to catalog-derived fallback
options.body: Use the related fallbacksFromModels direction as the canonical implementation, accepting that it reduces duplication but does not fully solve wildcard/auto provider-family semantics.

options.title: Keep flat fallbacks only
options.body: Decline new fallback config for now and document explicit fallbacks as the supported way to preserve provider and cost control.

recommendation.title: Design explicit family fallback contract
recommendation.body: Adopt an explicit ordered family/group contract, such as fallbackFamilies or equivalent, so users control provider and subscription-tier order without relying on ambiguous provider auto-selection.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to repeated ownership of model fallback behavior, config schema changes, and related docs/product-scope decisions.
